text:
anya: Hey folks — quick q. My mom's having surgery in June and I need to be primary caregiver for ~8–10 weeks. Does Redwood have a caregiver stipend or formal short-term reduced-hours option?

jordan (People Ops): Sorry to hear that, anya. Yes, we have two things that might help: a caregiver stipend pilot (up to $500/mo, taxable) and a "phased return / temporary part-time" program. Which do you want more details on? :pray:

anya: Both please. Trying to figure out whether to go full leave or reduce to like 0.8 FTE for a couple months. What are the manager approvals and payroll implications?

maria (Benefits): Hi @anya — caregiver stipend: it's a pilot for 2026 Q2, available to full-time employees who need short-term caregiving for a dependent (child, parent, spouse). Eligibility is 6–12 weeks, and we can approve up to $500/month. It's treated as taxable income and processed through payroll as a one-line stipend. We require a short attestation form and an estimated schedule.

maria (Benefits): Dependent Care FSA is separate if you have eligible expenses — pre-tax contributions are subject to IRS limits (check the benefits portal for current year limits). The stipend does not affect FSA eligibility, but you can't double-claim the same expense. Link: https://benefits.redwood.com/caregiver-pilot

jordan (People Ops): Phased return: manager sign-off + 1:1 with People Ops to document FTE change and duration. We create a temporary schedule (example: 0.8 FTE for 8 weeks) and a return-to-full-time date. Payroll needs the effective date before the monthly payroll cutoff (usually the 15th).

jordan (People Ops): Steps (high level):
- Employee submits phased-return request form to people-ops@redwood.com
- Manager approves in writing (reply to the request thread)
- People Ops sets org/HR record + notifies payroll with effective dates
- Benefits team confirms any impact to prorated benefits (rare for short periods)

devon (eng-manager): fwiw happy to support a temporary 0.8 plan for anya. We usually do 4-week checkpoints.

anya: Thanks — what's on the attestation form for the stipend? Will I need to show a doctor's note?

maria (Benefits): Attestation asks for: dependent relationship, start/end date estimate, brief description of caregiving needs, and preferred stipend amount (up to cap). For medical situations we request a clinician note only if the timeframe requested is >12 weeks or if the case involves extended FMLA paperwork. Most short, time-bound requests don't need a doctor's note.

jordan (People Ops): Payroll timeline note: if you want the stipend to start on June 1, submit everything by May 15 so payroll can code it for the June pay run. If you miss cutoff we can do an off-cycle adjustment but it takes longer.

anya: Great. I'll fill the forms tonight. Quick sample manager ack?
devon (eng-manager): Confirmed — I approve anya to move to 0.8 FTE from 2026-06-01 to 2026-07-31, with weekly check-ins.

jordan (People Ops): Perfect — @anya send the phased-return form + stipend attestation to people-ops@redwood.com and cc devon. We'll route to payroll and benefits and confirm receipt. Expect a confirmation email within 2 business days. :white_check_mark:

payroll-bot: Payroll note: to ensure stipend appears on paystub as "Caregiver Stipend" please include employee ID and exact dates. Off-cycle runs processed Tue/Thu; allow 3 business days.

anya: Thank you all — much appreciated.

maria (Benefits): Also: if you want help estimating the budget impact on your take-home pay for 0.8 FTE, reply here and I can send a quick example calculation.

anya: That would be helpful, thanks.

jordan (People Ops): I'll open a case and tag benefits for the estimate. Case #PO-2026-281.

anya: Awesome. :heart:

maria (Benefits): Sending estimate now via email.

jordan (People Ops): Closing loop here — let us know if you need anything else and good luck to your mom.

anya: Thanks again everyone.
